title: Warn in setup when Cargo's bin directory is not on PATH
summary: The cause is that setup.sh adds Cargo's bin to PATH only for its own process, and the final summary in xtask setup never says so. A user on a clean machine therefore hits "command not found" at the README's `cargo test` step (n6). The fix is a warning in setup's output that names the directory and the line to add. It targets the README reader on a fresh machine.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust in xtask.
Unit tests for the PATH check, with cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria check the warning appearing or not for given PATH values.
The warning covers both the --ci and normal paths and respects CARGO_HOME.
One focused change in setup's output.
The message is plain and self-explanatory.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The warning belongs in xtask's Rust setup output (the summary), not in setup.sh, because the project is Rust-only and the existing ~/.local/bin PATH hint is already there.

The check compares PATH entries as the setup process sees them. setup.sh prepends Cargo's bin to its own PATH, so xtask cannot tell whether the user's shell had it. The producer must therefore have setup.sh pass the original state through (for example an env var), or have the warning be unconditional whenever the shell's original PATH lacked it. This is why setup.sh has a small chance of changing.
The warning is informational and does not fail setup.

acceptance_criteria.text: xtask/src/main.rs has a pure helper that takes the PATH value and the Cargo home and says whether `<cargo home>/bin` is on PATH. CARGO_HOME is honoured, with `$HOME/.cargo` as the fallback. setup calls the helper in both the normal path and the --ci early return, so the warning shows either way.

When the directory is missing from PATH, the warning names the directory and gives a copyable line to add (for example `export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"`). It also says this is needed for the README's `cargo` commands. When the directory is on PATH, nothing extra is printed.

Unit tests in xtask cover three cases: the directory absent from PATH (warns), present (silent), and a custom CARGO_HOME. Run `cargo test -p xtask`, which must pass. `cargo clippy --all-targets` must be clean and `cargo fmt --check` must pass.

A reader following the README on a clean machine is told in setup's output, before the `cargo test` step, why `cargo` may not be found and how to fix it. The README's setup step is consistent with this message if it was touched.

out_of_scope: Editing the user's shell profile or running rustup-init without --no-modify-path
The other deferred items (n1-n5, n7, m6-m8)
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, or CI workflows
Changing the pinned rustup version or checksums
departures: The PATH that xtask sees may already include Cargo's bin because setup.sh prepends it, so the producer must carry the original state across. This adds some risk to verification beyond the reference.
